newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SURREY HAVE CHANCE TO ATONE FOR DISAPPOINTING SEASON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SURREY HAVE CHANCE TO ATONE FOR DISAPPOINTING SEASON.

text.p: Surrey, English cricket's perennial under-achievers, have a chance to atone for another disappointing season in Saturday's Benson and Hedges one-day final against Kent at Lord's.
Under their innovative Australian coach Dave Gilbert, Surrey started the season with high hopes in both the championship and the three-day one-day competitions.

But with the season at the halfway point, the London club are languishing in the bottom six of the championship, flagging in the Sunday league and were knocked out of the NatWest trophy on Wednesday after a feeble performance against Nottinghamshire.
"That won't affect morale," said captain Adam Hollioake, one of five Surrey players to represent England this season.
The Surrey skipper believes the absence of the club's three regular England batsmen Mark Butcher, Alec Stewart and Graham Thorpe has made it difficult to maintain consistent results.

Hollioake and his younger brother Ben, both born in Melbourne and both all-rounders, played leading parts in England's 3-0 whitewash of Australia in the one-day series but have been selected for the subsequent test matches.

The man keeping the Hollioakes out of the test team is Kent all-rounder Mark Ealham, who without looking quite test class with either bat or ball has done everything asked of him in the three test matches.
So too has paceman Dean Headley who took eight wickets in his only match of the series, the 268-run loss to Australia at Old Trafford which squared the series 1-1.
Martin McCague, a disappointment at test level, has bowled fast and well this season for Kent while Ealham and leg-spinner Paul Strang complete the stronger of the two attacks.
